system_overview: This specification models an algorithm to compute a rooted spanning tree of an undirected graph. The algorithm computes the parent relation and distance from a designated root node for every node in the graph. It effectively assumes all edges have weight 1. If the graph is not connected, nodes without a path to the root remain unattached (their parent is themselves). The algorithm repeatedly finds nodes whose distance can be improved via a neighbor and updates them.
actors_and_components: The system operates on an undirected graph defined by a set of nodes and a set of edges. There is a single designated root node. The algorithm is centralized: in each step, it nondeterministically selects a node and one of its neighbors, then updates the selected node's distance and parent if an improvement is possible.
state_variables: The system maintains two mappings over all nodes: (1) a parent function that maps each node to the node considered its parent in the spanning tree (the root and unreachable nodes map to themselves), and (2) a distance function that maps each node to a natural number representing its computed distance from the root.
initial_state: Every node's parent is set to itself. The root node's distance is set to 0. All other nodes' distances are set to a large constant that serves as a stand-in for infinity (this constant must be at least as large as the number of nodes).
actions: The algorithm has one action: choose a node and one of its graph neighbors such that the neighbor's distance plus one is strictly less than the node's current distance. Then choose a new distance value for the node that is strictly less than its current distance but at least the neighbor's distance plus one. Update the node's distance to this new value and set the node's parent to the chosen neighbor. The reason the algorithm allows setting the distance to any value in this range (rather than just the neighbor's distance plus one) is to support refinement by a distributed implementation where a node may receive stale information from neighbors.
safety_properties: When the algorithm terminates (no further transitions are enabled), the postcondition holds: for every node, one of three cases applies: (1) it is the root, with distance 0 and parent equal to itself; (2) it is unreachable, with distance equal to the maximum constant, parent equal to itself, and all of its neighbors also unreachable; or (3) it has a distance between 1 and the maximum minus one, its parent is one of its graph neighbors, and its distance equals its parent's distance plus one. The safety property states that this postcondition always holds upon termination.
liveness_properties: The algorithm eventually terminates: eventually, no further transitions are enabled. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The graph is specified by constants: the set of nodes, the set of edges (each edge is a two-element subset of nodes), the root node (which must be in the node set), and a maximum cardinality constant (a natural number at least as large as the number of nodes, used in place of infinity).
additional_assumptions: No self-loops are permitted (each edge has exactly two distinct endpoints). There is at most one edge between any pair of nodes. The algorithm is designed so that it can be refined by a distributed message-passing implementation.
